subject.title: Agent-to-Agent Communication Tools Have Parameter Conflicts

question: For plain `message(action="send")`, should OpenClaw hide poll creation fields from send-capable schemas, strip accidental poll fields at runtime, or continue rejecting content-bearing poll fields as explicit poll intent?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses the model-facing message-tool schema, shared outbound validation, and channel delivery contract, so automation should not choose the permanent contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Action-scope poll fields
options.body: Expose poll creation fields only for `poll` or channel-specific poll surfaces so plain sends cannot inherit them from the shared schema while strict poll validation remains intact.

options.title: Strip on send
options.body: Treat `action="send"` as authoritative and remove poll creation fields before delivery, improving send reliability while potentially masking a caller that meant to create a poll.

options.title: Keep strict guard
options.body: Preserve the shipped content-bearing rejection and require stronger live evidence before changing the shared message-tool contract.

recommendation.title: Action-scope poll fields
recommendation.body: Expose poll creation fields only for `poll` or channel-specific poll surfaces so plain sends cannot inherit them from the shared schema while strict poll validation remains intact.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged poll gating and schema consistency work is the strongest current history signal for the shared send/poll contract boundary.
